olympic.overview: Olympic National Park offers three distinct hiking environments: glacier-capped alpine ridges, temperate rainforests, and rugged Pacific coastline. Walkers can tackle the long High Divide Loop for views of Mount Olympus, explore the moss-draped trails of the Hoh Rain Forest, or navigate the tidal zones of the Wilderness Coast on a multi-day trek. The best conditions run from July through September when the high trails melt out and the weather is reliably dry.

months.4: Spring melt begins at middle elevations while the alpine trails still hold snow. The Sol Duc and Hoh valleys provide excellent, albeit wet, day hikes through old-growth timber.
months.7: The reliably dry window begins, melting out the high country. The long High Divide Loop and Hurricane Hill are fully accessible, offering expansive views of glaciers and peaks.

pakistan.overview: Pakistan's Karakoram range offers dramatic expedition trekking, dominated by the multi-week route up the Baltoro Glacier to K2 Base Camp. Shorter hikes reach the high pastures of Fairy Meadows beneath Nanga Parbat, while the Hunza Valley provides lower-elevation trails. The high-altitude routes require serious commitment, and the K2 trek mandates an approved guide and agency.

months.1: The high Karakoram is locked in deep winter snow, and the walking routes are out of reach.
months.2: Deep snow and bitter cold hold the mountains, and the trekking routes stay closed.
months.3: Snow still covers the passes and glaciers, keeping the high routes closed.
months.5: Lower trails and the hike up to Fairy Meadows begin to open, but the high glacier treks remain snowbound.
months.11: Heavy snow and bitter cold shut the mountains, ending the walking season.
months.12: Deep winter settles over the Karakoram, with the high routes buried and the valleys cold.

months.1: Drier weather leaves less mud on the steep steps of the short jungle walk to Ngardmau Waterfall.
months.2: February is among the drier months, so the steps to Ngardmau Waterfall are firmer and less muddy.
months.3: March keeps the dry spell going, with the short jungle path to the waterfall in its best shape.
months.4: April stays fairly dry, and the steps and jungle path to Ngardmau Waterfall are still manageable.
months.5: As rain increases in May, the short jungle trail and steps to the waterfall begin to get muddy and slippery.
months.6: Heavy tropical rain in June leaves the steps and jungle path to the waterfall muddy and slippery.
months.7: July's heavy rain keeps the jungle path and steps to Ngardmau Waterfall slick.
months.8: August rain continues to make the steep steps to the waterfall muddy and slippery.
months.9: September rain keeps the short jungle trail and steps wet and slippery.
months.10: Rain stays frequent in October, so the trail and steps remain muddy.
months.11: November brings drier conditions, making the short jungle walk to Ngardmau Waterfall less muddy.
months.12: December is dry enough for the waterfall walk, with less mud on the steep steps.

months.1: The dry weather makes this an excellent time to climb Mount Tapyas or Taraw Cliff for clear views over the bays.
months.2: Dry, clear days continue, with firm steps on Mount Tapyas and good visibility from Taraw Cliff. Dawn is still the coolest time to climb.
months.3: Dry weather holds, though the heat is building. Dawn or dusk climbs of Mount Tapyas stay the most comfortable.
months.7: Heavy monsoon rain and storms leave the steep trails muddy and the limestone scrambles dangerously slick.
months.8: Monsoon storms continue, and the limestone at Taraw Cliff is slick enough to make the scramble unsafe.
months.9: Rain and storms linger, keeping the trails muddy and the limestone slick.

panama.overview: Panama offers tropical hiking ranging from the cloud forests of the western highlands to the lowland rainforests near the canal. The best-known routes center around Boquete, including the long hike up Volcán Barú for views that can stretch to both oceans on a clear day. Trails are often muddy and humid, with the dry season providing the most reliable conditions.

months.2: Dry weather continues, with firm trails and clear mornings in the highlands around Boquete.
months.3: The dry spell holds, keeping the Boquete trails firm and the volcano slopes clear in the morning.
months.4: Late dry-season conditions still favor the Boquete trails, with cloud starting to build over the volcano by afternoon.
months.7: Regular downpours keep the highland trails slick, and lowland rainforest walks are best timed for the mornings.
months.8: Wet weather continues to turn highland trails to mud, with morning the best window before the clouds close in.
months.10: Rain stays heavy, with the wettest conditions of the year making the mountain trails deeply muddy.
months.11: The heavy rains linger, so mountain trails stay muddy and cloud often hides the views.

pantanal.overview: The Pantanal is a vast wetland where walking is limited to short, flat trails and raised boardwalks. These easy paths lead through gallery forests and open marshes on foot. The best conditions for walking run from July to September when the ground is dry.

months.7: Dry conditions make this a good month to walk the dirt trails and boardwalks.

papua-new-guinea.overview: Papua New Guinea is defined by the Kokoda Track, a grueling 60-mile, eight-day trek through dense jungle and steep, muddy ridges. Walkers come for the wartime history and the deep, remote wilderness of the Owen Stanley Range. Beyond Kokoda, the highland valleys offer shorter day hikes to remote villages and birding sites. The walking is best from May to September when the trails are driest, as heavy rains turn the paths into deep mud for much of the rest of the year. A permit is required for the Kokoda Track.

months.10: Humidity and rain begin to increase, softening the trails and making the steep jungle ascents harder work.

paris.overview: Paris is a flat-city base for day walks by train: the vast Fontainebleau forest and sections of the GR11 loop. Walkers find gentle day hikes through ancient woodlands, sandstone ridges, and countryside. The city itself offers flat urban park strolls.

months.1: Winter brings grey skies and chilly temperatures to the Île-de-France. The Fontainebleau forest trails remain open but can be muddy, requiring warm layers for a woodland walk.
months.2: The woods are still bare and temperatures remain brisk. It is a good time for an easy day hike along the GR11, though trails are often damp.
months.9: Early fall is a sweet spot for walking the Île-de-France. The temperatures cool, making the day hikes highly enjoyable.
months.12: Winter settles in with brisk, grey days. The forest paths are stark, offering a brisk walk for those dressed for the cold.
